hints: Repeated XOR combinations can produce the same result.
Build a linearly independent XOR basis.
A basis of rank r represents exactly 2^r distinct XORs, including zero.
analogy: Each independent basis vector is a switch that doubles the number of reachable XOR values.
example: For [3,6,5], 5=3 XOR 6, so rank is 2 and the distinct results are 0,3,5,6.
algorithm: Insert each value into a binary XOR basis by eliminating its highest set bit with existing pivots until it becomes zero or introduces a new pivot. If r pivots remain, print 2^r.
correctness: The basis spans exactly the original subset XORs. Independence makes all 2^r choices of basis vectors yield different results, including the empty choice.
complexity: For n values and B bits, O(nB) time and O(B) space.
